# GTFS Guru

> A GTFS validator written in Rust. It checks transit feeds (GTFS) against 110
> validation rules and runs entirely on the user's own machine — in the browser
> via WebAssembly, on the desktop, from the command line, from Python, or in CI.
> Free and open source under Apache 2.0.

GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) is the file format transit agencies
publish so that journey planners such as Google Maps, Apple Maps, Transit and
Citymapper can show their schedules. A GTFS validator catches errors in that
feed before it is published.

GTFS Guru is a Rust rewrite of the canonical Java validator maintained by
MobilityData. It reproduces the same rules and notice codes, so a report from
either tool describes the same feed problems.

## Answers to common questions

- **How do I validate a GTFS feed?** Drop the `.zip` on <https://gtfs.guru/>
  (it never leaves the browser), or run `gtfs-guru -i feed.zip -o ./report`.
- **Is it free?** Yes. Apache 2.0, no usage limits, no paid tier.
- **Is my feed uploaded anywhere?** No. Browser validation runs in WebAssembly
  on the visitor's device; the desktop, CLI and Python paths are local too. The
  only network call the site can make with a feed is the optional URL fetch
  proxy, used when a feed host blocks cross-origin browser requests.
- **How does it compare with the Java validator?** See the table below.
- **How do I run it in CI?** Use the GitHub Action, or the CLI with
  `--fail-on error`. Both can emit SARIF for GitHub code scanning.

## GTFS Guru vs the canonical Java validator

| Measure | Canonical Java validator | GTFS Guru (Rust) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MBTA feed benchmark | 10.60s | 2.32s (4.6x faster) |
| OVapi Netherlands feed benchmark | 65.18s | 9.75s (6.7x faster) |
| Small feeds | JVM startup dominates | up to 100x faster |
| Peak memory | ~1.5 GB | ~150 MB |
| Runtime requirement | Java runtime | standalone binary, no runtime |
| Browser | not available | WebAssembly, runs in the tab |
| Python | wrapper around the JAR | native package (`pip install gtfs-guru`) |
| CI output | JSON, HTML | SARIF, JSON, HTML, plus a GitHub Action |
| Validation rules | canonical rule set | 110 validators, 190 notice codes |
| Licence | Apache 2.0 | Apache 2.0 |

Benchmarks were run on an Apple M3 Pro with a warm page cache, each tool
validating end to end and writing its normal reports. Numbers and method:
<https://github.com/abasis-ltd/gtfs.guru#-performance>

## How to use it

Browser (nothing to install):

1. Open <https://gtfs.guru/>
2. Drop a `gtfs.zip` on the validator, paste a feed URL, or click
   "Try an example feed"
3. Read the report; download it as JSON or HTML, or copy a shareable link

Command line:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abasis-ltd/gtfs.guru/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
gtfs-guru -i feed.zip -o ./report              # JSON + HTML reports
gtfs-guru -i feed.zip -o ./report --fail-on error   # exit 2 on any error
gtfs-guru -i feed.zip -o ./report --sarif report.sarif.json
gtfs-guru -i feed.zip -o ./report --badge badge.json
gtfs-guru --stdout -i feed.zip | jq .
```

Python:

```python
import gtfs_guru

report = gtfs_guru.validate("feed.zip")
if not report.is_valid:
    print(report.error_count)
    report.save_html("report.html")
```

GitHub Actions:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: abasis-ltd/gtfs.guru/action@v1
  with:
    feed: feed.zip
    fail-on: error
```

## Docs

- [Homepage and browser validator](https://gtfs.guru/): drag-and-drop validation, no upload
- [How to validate a GTFS feed](https://gtfs.guru/how-to-validate-gtfs.html): step by step
- [Why a GTFS feed gets rejected](https://gtfs.guru/why-is-my-gtfs-rejected.html): the common causes
- [How to create a GTFS file](https://gtfs.guru/how-to-create-gtfs-file.html): building a feed from scratch
- [Getting a bus onto Google Maps](https://gtfs.guru/how-to-get-my-bus-on-google-maps.html): the submission process
- [How often to update a GTFS feed](https://gtfs.guru/how-often-update-gtfs.html): publishing cadence
- [Where to find GTFS feeds](https://gtfs.guru/where-to-find-gtfs-feeds.html): public feed sources
- [GTFS vs GTFS Realtime](https://gtfs.guru/gtfs-vs-gtfs-realtime.html): what each format covers
- [What GTFS stands for](https://gtfs.guru/what-does-gtfs-stand-for.html): the acronym and its history
- [What GTFS is used for](https://gtfs.guru/what-is-gtfs-used-for.html): who consumes the data
- [Who uses GTFS](https://gtfs.guru/who-uses-gtfs.html): agencies, apps and analysts
- [Is GTFS free](https://gtfs.guru/is-gtfs-free.html): licensing of the format and of feeds
- [All guides](https://gtfs.guru/faq.html): index of the above

## Reference

- [Source code](https://github.com/abasis-ltd/gtfs.guru): Rust workspace, Apache 2.0
- [Validation rules](https://github.com/abasis-ltd/gtfs.guru/blob/main/docs/rules.md): all 110 validators and 190 notice codes
- [CLI usage](https://github.com/abasis-ltd/gtfs.guru/blob/main/docs/usage.md): every flag, exit codes, report layout
- [Python API](https://github.com/abasis-ltd/gtfs.guru/blob/main/docs/python_api.md): the `gtfs_guru` package
- [WebAssembly](https://github.com/abasis-ltd/gtfs.guru/blob/main/docs/wasm.md): embedding the validator in a page
- [GitHub Action](https://github.com/abasis-ltd/gtfs.guru/blob/main/action/README.md): inputs, outputs, badges
- [Compact LLM guide](https://github.com/abasis-ltd/gtfs.guru/blob/main/docs/llm.md): copy-paste reference kept short for context windows
- [Machine-readable notice schema](https://github.com/abasis-ltd/gtfs.guru/blob/main/docs/rules.md): export with `gtfs-guru --export-notices-schema`
- [Releases](https://github.com/abasis-ltd/gtfs.guru/releases/latest): binaries for macOS, Windows and Linux
- [PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/gtfs-guru/): `pip install gtfs-guru`
- [Crates.io package](https://crates.io/crates/gtfs-guru): `cargo install gtfs-guru`
